questions.question: Who among the following is responsible for implementing decisions made by a Municipal Corporation’s council and standing committees in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Municipal Commissioner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Municipal Commissioner** is the chief executive officer of a municipal corporation in India.
 
• He/she is responsible for implementing the decisions made by the municipal council and standing committees.
 
• The Municipal Commissioner is typically appointed by the **state government** and is a senior officer of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS).
 
• The role involves overseeing the daily administration, including public health, sanitation, urban development, and revenue collection.
 
• The Municipal Commissioner ensures the effective execution of policies and programs within the jurisdiction of the municipal corporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Municipal Corporation:**

 
 
• A municipal corporation is a governing body for large urban areas in India, established under state laws.
 
• It is responsible for providing civic amenities such as water supply, sewage, roads, and public health facilities.
 
• The governing body includes elected representatives (councilors) and an administrative head (Municipal Commissioner).
 
 
 
• **Standing Committees:**
 
 
• Standing committees are specialized groups within the municipal corporation responsible for specific functions like finance, health, and education.
 
• These committees assist the council in decision-making and policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **Mayor vs. Municipal Commissioner:**
 
 
• The Mayor is the ceremonial head of the municipal corporation, usually elected by councilors or citizens.
 
• The Municipal Commissioner holds executive authority and is responsible for implementing decisions and managing day-to-day operations.
 
 
 
• **State Control:**
 
 
• The state government has significant control over municipal corporations, including appointing the Municipal Commissioner.
 
• This ensures alignment between state policies and municipal governance.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions the Fundamental Duty of defending the country and rendering national service when called upon to do so?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A (d)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 51A (d)** of the Constitution of India mandates that it is the **Fundamental Duty** of every Indian citizen to "defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so."
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties are enshrined under **Part IVA** of the Constitution.
 
• The objective of incorporating Fundamental Duties is to remind citizens of their moral obligations toward the nation and to uphold the spirit of patriotism.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**

 
 
• It is also known as the "Mini Constitution" of India due to the significant changes it brought to the Constitution.
 
• It introduced **Fundamental Duties**, added the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" to the Preamble, and curtailed the power of the judiciary, among other changes.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee**
 
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was constituted in 1976 to recommend the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
• It was named after Swaran Singh, the then Minister of External Affairs.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• They serve as a moral code of conduct for citizens to contribute positively to society and the nation.
 
 
 
• **Part IVA of the Constitution**
 
 
• Part IVA was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• It contains only one Article, Article 51A, which enumerates the Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: In March 2025, what important decision did the Supreme Court of India make regarding disability rights?

options.text: It allowed only private companies to hire persons with disabilities.
It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.
It removed reservations for persons with disabilities.
It banned all exams for persons with disabilities.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India, in March 2025, declared that **disability rights are an integral part of fundamental rights** under the Indian Constitution.
 
• This landmark decision emphasized the enforcement of the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016**, ensuring equality, dignity, and inclusion for persons with disabilities.
 
• The judgment underscored Article 21 of the Constitution, which guarantees the **right to life with dignity**, and linked it to the rights of individuals with disabilities.
 
• It mandated that public and private entities must ensure **reasonable accommodations** for persons with disabilities to eliminate discrimination.
 
• The ruling reinforced the idea that **accessibility, equal opportunities, and non-discrimination** are essential for fostering an inclusive society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPwD Act):**

 
 
• It replaced the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights, and Full Participation) Act, 1995.
 
• The Act recognizes 21 types of disabilities, including mental illness, autism, and dwarfism.
 
• It ensures rights such as education, employment, and social security for persons with disabilities.
 
• It mandates a reservation of **4% in government jobs** and **5% in educational institutions** for persons with benchmark disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Fundamental rights are guaranteed under Articles 12–35 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 21 guarantees the **right to life and personal liberty**, which includes the right to live with dignity.
 
• Equality before law (Article 14) and prohibition of discrimination (Article 15) are key provisions supporting disability rights.
 
 
 
• **Reasonable Accommodation:**
 
 
• It refers to necessary and appropriate modifications to ensure persons with disabilities can enjoy their rights equally.
 
• Examples include ramps in buildings, assistive technologies, or extended time during examinations.
 
 
 
• **Global Framework on Disability Rights:**
 
 
• The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) was adopted in 2006.
 
• India ratified the UNCRPD in 2007, committing to its principles of equality, non-discrimination, and accessibility.

questions.question: What is the dual role of the highest judicial officer in a district?

options.text: Nyaya Panchayat head for civil cases and Gram Kutchery head for criminal cases
District Judge for civil cases and Sessions Judge for criminal cases
Chief Judicial Magistrate for civil cases and Munsiff for criminal cases
Subordinate Judge for civil cases and Metropolitan Magistrate for criminal cases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**District Judge for civil cases and Sessions Judge for criminal cases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The highest judicial officer in a district performs a dual role as **District Judge for civil cases** and **Sessions Judge for criminal cases**.
 
• The District Judge is responsible for adjudicating civil disputes, including property disputes, contract disputes, and family matters.
 
• The Sessions Judge handles criminal cases, which include trials for serious offenses such as murder, robbery, and rape.
 
• The Sessions Court is empowered to impose the maximum sentence prescribed under the law, including life imprisonment or the death penalty in rare cases.
 
• The dual role ensures efficient functioning of judicial proceedings at the district level and proper allocation of responsibilities between civil and criminal jurisdictions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **District Judiciary Structure:**

 
 
• The district judiciary system operates at the district level, with the District Judge being the highest judicial authority.
 
• Subordinate courts such as Munsiff Courts and Magistrate Courts assist in handling lower-level cases.
 
 
 
• **Sessions Court:**
 
 
• The Sessions Court is the principal criminal court in a district.
 
• It can try offenses under the Indian Penal Code and other criminal laws.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Appointments:**
 
 
• District Judges and Sessions Judges are appointed by the High Court of the respective state.
 
• Promotions are based on merit and seniority within the judiciary system.
 
 
 
• **Nyaya Panchayat:**
 
 
• Nyaya Panchayats are village-level courts established to handle minor disputes and offenses.
 
• They work as alternative dispute resolution mechanisms but are not part of the formal judiciary.

questions.question: When appointing judges to the Supreme Court, the President must consult which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Chief Justice of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 124(2) of the Indian Constitution mandates the President of India to consult the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** while appointing judges to the Supreme Court.
 
• The practice of consultation with the CJI ensures a system of checks and balances in the judicial appointment process.
 
• This consultation is binding on the President, as established by the Supreme Court’s judgments in the **Second Judges’ Case (1993)** and the **Third Judges’ Case (1998)**.
 
• The collegium system, comprising the CJI and senior judges of the Supreme Court, plays a significant role in recommending names for judicial appointments.
 
• The President, while consulting the CJI, does not act solely on their advice but also takes into account the recommendations made by the **Supreme Court Collegium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collegium System:**

 
 
• It is a system used for the appointment and transfer of judges in the Supreme Court and High Courts of India.
 
• The collegium comprises the CJI and the four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• It was introduced through the **Second Judges’ Case (1993)**, which gave primacy to the judiciary over the executive in judicial appointments.
 
 
 
• **Second and Third Judges’ Cases:**
 
 
• The **Second Judges’ Case (1993)** established the principle that the Chief Justice of India’s opinion holds primacy in judicial appointments.
 
• The **Third Judges’ Case (1998)** clarified the role of the collegium and expanded its composition to include four senior-most judges along with the CJI.
 
 
 
• **Article 124 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• It deals with the establishment and composition of the Supreme Court, including the appointment of judges.
 
• Clause (2) of Article 124 specifies the consultation process for appointing judges.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President appoints Supreme Court judges based on the recommendations of the collegium.
 
• However, the President can seek clarification or reconsideration of the recommendation, but this is rare and usually non-binding.

questions.question: What was the cutoff date for migrants to be eligible under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 (CAA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wed Dec 31 2014 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 (CAA) specifies **December 31, 2014** as the cutoff date for eligibility of migrants seeking citizenship under its provisions.
 
• The Act allows citizenship for migrants from **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan** belonging to Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, and Christian communities.
 
• The CAA aims to provide citizenship to religious minorities who faced **religious persecution** in these countries before the cutoff date.
 
• It applies to migrants who entered India before **December 31, 2014, without valid travel documents or overstayed their visas.**
 
• The Act does not apply to **Muslim migrants** and has faced significant debates and protests over its exclusionary criteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955**

 
 
• The Citizenship Act of 1955 governs the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship.
 
• It has been amended several times, including major changes through the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019.
 
• Citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, or incorporation of territory under the Act.
 
 
 
• **Religious Persecution**
 
 
• Religious persecution refers to systematic mistreatment of individuals based on their religious beliefs.
 
• The CAA was enacted to address the plight of religious minorities facing persecution in neighboring countries.
 
 
 
• **Legal Challenges to CAA**
 
 
• The Act has faced numerous petitions in the Supreme Court of India, questioning its constitutionality.
 
• Critics argue that it violates the secular principles of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **National Register of Citizens (NRC)**
 
 
• The NRC is a register of Indian citizens aimed at identifying illegal migrants.
 
• The CAA has been linked to the NRC, leading to concerns about discrimination against specific communities.

questions.question: How does the writ jurisdiction of the High Courts differ from that of the Supreme Court?

options.text: High Courts require prior approval from the Supreme Court before issuing writs.
High Courts can issue writs only against state governments, not the Centre.
High Courts can issue writs only in appellate cases, not in original jurisdiction.
High Courts can issue writs for purposes beyond Fundamental Rights, unlike the Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High Courts can issue writs for purposes beyond Fundamental Rights, unlike the Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **High Courts have broader writ jurisdiction** as they can issue writs not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for other legal rights.
 
• The Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction under **Article 32** of the Constitution is restricted to the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• High Courts derive their writ jurisdiction from **Article 226**, which explicitly allows them to issue writs for any other purpose besides Fundamental Rights.
 
• This expanded scope enables High Courts to address issues such as administrative orders, statutory duties, and violations of legal rights, providing greater flexibility.
 
• Both courts can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writ Jurisdiction Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** Used to ensure a person's release from unlawful detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** Directs public officials or bodies to perform their duties.
 
• **Prohibition:** Prevents lower courts from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** Allows higher courts to quash orders of lower courts if they acted beyond their jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** Questions the legal authority of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Article 32 vs Article 226:**
 
 
• **Article 32:** Grants the Supreme Court exclusive powers to issue writs for Fundamental Rights enforcement.
 
• **Article 226:** Provides High Courts with expanded writ jurisdiction for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
• Article 226 is considered broader in scope than Article 32.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Enshrined under Part III of the Constitution of India.
 
• Include rights such as equality, freedom of speech, protection against discrimination, and right to constitutional remedies.
 
• Writs are a mechanism to enforce these rights.
 
 
 
• **Legal Rights:**
 
 
• These are rights granted by statutes or laws, such as property rights, contract rights, etc.
 
• High Courts can issue writs for their enforcement under Article 226.

questions.question: An award made by a Lok Adalat has the same status as a ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Court decree**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An award made by a Lok Adalat is considered to have the same legal status as a **decree of a Civil Court.**
 
• It is deemed final and binding on all parties involved, and no appeal lies against it in any court of law.
 
• The Lok Adalat system works under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, promoting alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
• It resolves disputes through conciliation and compromise, offering an accessible and cost-effective mechanism for justice.
 
• Once a dispute is settled by Lok Adalat, it is enforceable as a Civil Court decree under Section 21 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat**

 
 
• Lok Adalat translates to "People's Court" and is an integral part of the Indian judicial system.
 
• It is an alternative dispute resolution forum aimed at reducing the burden on regular courts.
 
• It is free of cost and does not require payment of court fees by the disputing parties.
 
• Lok Adalats are organized at various levels, including state, district, and taluk levels.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**
 
 
• This Act provides the statutory basis for the establishment of Lok Adalats in India.
 
• The Act aims to provide free and competent legal services to weaker sections of society.
 
• It promotes the resolution of disputes amicably and ensures that justice is accessible to all.
 
 
 
• **Types of Cases Handled by Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Cases related to civil disputes, including matrimonial and property disputes.
 
• Compoundable criminal cases and cases under the Motor Vehicles Act.
 
• Disputes related to bank recovery, labor matters, and public utility services.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Ensures speedy justice and reduces the backlog of cases in regular courts.
 
• It is a cost-effective and informal forum for dispute resolution.
 
• Encourages amicable settlement through mutual consent and eliminates procedural complexities.

questions.question: What is the maximum time limit for a co-operative society to conduct its annual general meeting after the close of the financial year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 months**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The maximum time limit for a co-operative society to conduct its annual general meeting after the close of the financial year is **6 months**.
 
• This provision ensures transparency and accountability in the functioning of co-operative societies.
 
• The requirement is governed under the **Co-operative Societies Act**, which varies slightly across different states in India.
 
• The AGM is crucial for presenting audited financial statements, electing office bearers, and discussing key resolutions.
 
• Non-compliance with the stipulated time frame may result in penalties or legal consequences for the society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Co-operative Societies Act:**

 
 
• The Act provides the legal framework for the registration, management, and functioning of co-operative societies in India.
 
• While the Central Co-operative Societies Act exists, states have their own laws to govern co-operative societies within their jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Annual General Meeting (AGM):**
 
 
• An AGM is a statutory meeting where members review the society's performance and financial health.
 
• Key agenda items include approval of audited accounts, election of office bearers, and discussion of future plans.
 
 
 
• **Audited Financial Statements:**
 
 
• Financial statements must be audited by a certified auditor before being presented at the AGM.
 
• Auditing ensures accuracy and compliance with accounting standards.
 
 
 
• **Penalties for Non-Compliance:**
 
 
• Failure to conduct the AGM within the stipulated timeframe may attract penalties under the respective Co-operative Societies Act.
 
• Such penalties can include fines, suspension of society operations, or removal of office bearers.

questions.question: What was the key purpose of amending the Legal Services Authorities Act in 2002?

options.text: To merge Lok Adalats with High Courts
To establish permanent Lok Adalats for public utility service disputes
To replace all regular courts with Lok Adalats
To allow Lok Adalats to handle criminal cases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To establish permanent Lok Adalats for public utility service disputes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, was amended in 2002 to establish **permanent Lok Adalats** for resolving disputes concerning public utility services.
 
• Permanent Lok Adalats (PLAs) were introduced to provide **speedy, cost-effective, and amicable settlement** of disputes.
 
• The amendment focused on public utility services, including **transport, postal services, telecommunication, and water supply**, among others.
 
• Under this amendment, permanent Lok Adalats were empowered to handle disputes **prior to litigation**, ensuring dispute resolution without formal court proceedings.
 
• PLAs were given the authority to pass awards that are **final and binding**, provided the disputes do not involve serious criminal offenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalats**

 
 
• Lok Adalats are **alternative dispute resolution mechanisms** in India, organized under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• They aim to reduce the burden on regular courts by resolving disputes through **conciliation and compromise**.
 
• Decisions made in Lok Adalats are **deemed as decrees of civil courts** and are binding on all parties.
 
 
 
• **Public Utility Services**
 
 
• Services such as electricity, water, transport, postal services, and telecommunications are considered **public utility services**.
 
• The 2002 amendment to the Legal Services Authorities Act focused on protecting consumer rights in these essential services.
 
 
 
• **Composition of Permanent Lok Adalats**
 
 
• Each permanent Lok Adalat consists of a **chairman** (a retired judicial officer) and two other members with relevant expertise.
 
• The chairman ensures the proceedings are conducted fairly and impartially.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction of Permanent Lok Adalats**
 
 
• PLAs can resolve disputes where the value of the claim does not exceed **Rs. 1 crore**.
 
• Criminal cases involving non-compoundable offenses are **outside the jurisdiction** of Lok Adalats.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the formation of Union Public Service Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 315**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Union and Public Service Commissions for the States.
 
• The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a constitutional body that conducts examinations for appointments to the services of the Union.
 
• It is responsible for recruiting candidates for All India Services, Central Services, and other government posts under the Union.
 
• Article 315 ensures that the Public Service Commissions function independently, free from executive interference.
 
• The provisions under Article 315 aim to maintain transparency and meritocracy in the recruitment process for government positions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

 
 
• The UPSC is governed by Part XIV of the Indian Constitution under the title "Services under the Union and the States."
 
• The commission's role includes conducting examinations like the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and others.
 
• It also advises the President of India on matters related to recruitment, transfers, and disciplinary actions.
 
 
 
• **State Public Service Commissions**
 
 
• Each state in India has its own Public Service Commission to conduct recruitment for state-level services.
 
• These commissions function under the provisions of Articles 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Independence of Public Service Commissions**
 
 
• The members of the UPSC and State Public Service Commissions are appointed by the President or the Governor, respectively.
 
• Their independence is ensured by provisions related to security of tenure and conditions of service.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Articles**
 
 
• **Article 316:** Deals with the appointment and term of office of members of the Public Service Commissions.
 
• **Article 317:** Provides for the removal and suspension of a member of the Public Service Commission.
 
• **Article 318:** Empowers the President or Governor to make regulations regarding the conditions of service for members.

questions.question: In the Indian parliamentary system, who has the authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha before its term expires?

options.text: The Prime Minister advises the President to dissolve it.
The Council of Ministers passes a resolution.
The Chief Justice of India orders dissolution.
The Speaker of Lok Sabha takes the decision.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Prime Minister advises the President to dissolve it.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Indian parliamentary system, the **President of India** holds the formal authority to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• The dissolution of the Lok Sabha typically occurs **on the advice of the Prime Minister** and the Council of Ministers.
 
• This advice is binding on the President as per the principles of a parliamentary democracy where the President acts on the advice of the Cabinet.
 
• Dissolution can occur **before the completion of the Lok Sabha's five-year term** or upon its natural expiry.
 
• This process is crucial for initiating **fresh general elections** and ensuring democratic continuity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's Parliament and is composed of representatives directly elected by the people of India.
 
• It has a term of **five years**, unless dissolved sooner.
 
• It is responsible for enacting laws, controlling finances, and scrutinizing the work of the executive.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution of Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• Dissolution refers to the complete termination of the Lok Sabha's current term, leading to general elections.
 
• It can be classified into **automatic dissolution** (when the term ends) or **premature dissolution** (upon the Prime Minister's advice).
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President of India, as the constitutional head, formally dissolves the Lok Sabha.
 
• The President acts based on the advice of the Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Dissolution:**
 
 
• Dissolution ensures the periodic renewal of the democratic mandate through elections.
 
• It provides an opportunity for the electorate to evaluate the performance of the government.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the Supreme Court judgement delivered in April 2025 in a case involving the use of Urdu on a municipal signboard in Maharashtra?

1. The Supreme Court overturned the Bombay High Court's decision that forbade the use of Urdu on municipal signboards.

2. The Court held that language must reflect the religion of the majority in a particular region.

3.The bench recognised Urdu as part of India's Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb and criticised prejudice against languages.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, the Supreme Court delivered a landmark judgment concerning the use of Urdu on municipal signboards in Maharashtra.
 
• The Court recognised Urdu as an integral part of India's cultural heritage, specifically its Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb (syncretic culture).
 
• The bench criticised any form of prejudice or discrimination against languages and upheld linguistic diversity as central to India's identity.
 
• The judgment did not impose language restrictions based on religious or regional majorities, focusing instead on inclusivity.
 
• It overturned misconceptions tied to linguistic usage and called for mutual respect towards all Indian languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga-Jamuni Tehzeeb:**

 
 
• A term denoting the harmonious blending of Hindu and Muslim cultures in northern India.
 
• It reflects the region’s shared traditions, languages, arts, and cuisines.
 
• Urdu, among other languages, is considered a cultural bridge in this syncretic tradition.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court's Role in Language Matters:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has historically upheld linguistic rights under Article 29 and 30 of the Constitution.
 
• It ensures protection against linguistic discrimination and promotes India's multilingual identity.
 
 
 
• **Urdu Language:**
 
 
• Urdu is one of the scheduled languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It has a rich literary heritage and is widely spoken in parts of India, Pakistan, and other South Asian regions.
 
 
 
• **Article 29 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Guarantees the protection of cultural and linguistic rights of minorities.
 
• Ensures that no citizen is denied access to cultural resources based on language.

questions.question: Why is decentralised planning considered advantageous in the Panchayati Raj system in India?

options.text: It allows local communities to tailor need-based development initiatives.
It centralises power in the hands of a few state officials.
It limits community participation in development planning.
It slows down the decision-making process, hindering development.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It allows local communities to tailor need-based development initiatives.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Decentralised planning** empowers local communities to identify and address specific developmental needs, ensuring a more targeted approach to resource allocation.
 
• It enhances **community participation** in governance, creating a sense of ownership among citizens over developmental projects.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system fosters **bottom-up planning**, enabling grassroots-level involvement in decision-making and policy implementation.
 
• It ensures better accountability and transparency as decision-making is closer to the people, making it easier to monitor and evaluate progress.
 
• Decentralisation reduces dependency on centralised authorities and encourages **capacity building** at the local level, promoting sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Panchayati Raj System:**

 
 
• It is a system of local self-government in rural India introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
 
• The three-tier structure consists of Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zila Parishad (district level).
 
• It aims to decentralise governance and empower rural areas with administrative and financial autonomy.
 
 
 
• **Decentralisation:**
 
 
• It refers to the delegation of decision-making power from central authorities to lower levels of administration.
 
• Decentralisation promotes democratic participation, administrative efficiency, and resource optimisation.
 
 
 
• **Need-Based Development:**
 
 
• This approach prioritises initiatives that directly address the specific needs and priorities of a community.
 
• It ensures that resources are utilised effectively to achieve maximum impact on local welfare.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 73rd Amendment:**
 
 
• The amendment provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions, ensuring their continuity and greater accountability.
 
• It introduced a provision for regular elections and reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Decentralised Planning:**
 
 
• Lack of financial resources and technical expertise at the grassroots level can hinder effective implementation.
 
• Coordination among different levels of government is crucial for the success of decentralised initiatives.

questions.question: In which year was the provision for the free legal aid to the poor added to the Directive Principles of the State Policy of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1976**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provision for **free legal aid to the poor** was added to the **Directive Principles of State Policy** in the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• This amendment introduced **Article 39A**, which directs the State to promote justice on the basis of equal opportunity and provide free legal aid to ensure that no citizen is denied access to justice due to economic or other disabilities.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP) are non-justiciable guidelines for the government to ensure socio-economic welfare and justice.
 
• The 42nd Amendment is often referred to as the **“Mini Constitution”** because it introduced significant changes to the Constitution, including provisions related to education, environment, and justice.
 
• This amendment played a crucial role in strengthening the **welfare state** ideology and ensuring social justice for marginalized sections of society.
 
• The concept of free legal aid was influenced by the United Nations’ **Declaration of Human Rights**, which emphasizes equal access to justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1978**__

 __
 
• This year is significant for the **44th Amendment Act**, which reversed some provisions of the 42nd Amendment but did not relate to free legal aid.
 
• The 44th Amendment restored certain rights and protections, such as the provision for property rights under Article 300A.
 
 
 
• **2011**__
 __
 
• No major constitutional amendments related to free legal aid or Directive Principles occurred in this year.
 
• This year is more associated with **judicial and legislative developments**, such as the introduction of certain social welfare schemes and acts.
 
 
 
• **2002**__
 
 
• The **86th Amendment Act** was passed in this year, which added the provision for free and compulsory education for children under Article 21A.
 
• This amendment was important for education but had no connection to free legal aid.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions the Fundamental Duty of safeguarding public property and abjuring violence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A (i)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A** outlines the Fundamental Duties of citizens under Part IV-A of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• Article 51A (i) specifically mentions the duty of every citizen of India to **safeguard public property** and to **abjure violence**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**.
 
• These duties aim to remind citizens of their responsibility to contribute to the **nation's well-being** and ensure a harmonious social environment.
 
• The provision under Article 51A (i) is crucial for promoting a sense of responsibility among citizens to protect public assets and ensure that violence is avoided in public life.
 
• Public property refers to assets owned collectively by society, such as **parks, government buildings, public transport, and infrastructure**.
 
• Abjuring violence is essential for maintaining **peace and order** in society, ensuring that differences are resolved through non-violent means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 51A (h)**__

 __
 
• Article 51A (h) mandates citizens to develop the **scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform**.
 
• This duty emphasizes fostering a culture of **critical thinking and rationality** among Indian citizens.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (k)**__
 __
 
• Article 51A (k) obligates parents or guardians to provide **opportunities for education to their children** or wards between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This duty is in alignment with the **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (j)**__
 
 
• Article 51A (j) enjoins citizens to strive towards **excellence in all spheres** of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of achievement.
 
• This duty encourages citizens to work towards both **personal growth** and the **nation's development**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction is correct?

options.text: It extends to both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
It is exclusive and cannot be exercised by the High Courts.
It can only be invoked for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
It allows the Court to issue writs only against the Central Government.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It can only be invoked for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court’s **writ jurisdiction** is provided under **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined under **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, including rights such as **Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Constitutional Remedies**, etc.
 
• The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is considered a crucial mechanism for ensuring the protection of citizens' rights and maintaining the rule of law.
 
• The types of writs that can be issued include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto**.
 
• Article 32 is often referred to as the **"Heart and Soul of the Constitution"**, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, due to its significant role in safeguarding Fundamental Rights.
 
• Unlike the High Courts, the Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction is limited to matters involving Fundamental Rights and does not extend to other legal rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: It extends to both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect because the Supreme Court’s writ jurisdiction under **Article 32** is restricted to the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** only. It does not extend to other legal rights.
 
• However, High Courts under **Article 226** can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It is exclusive and cannot be exercised by the High Courts.**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect as **High Courts**, under **Article 226**, also have writ jurisdiction, which is broader than the Supreme Court’s jurisdiction under Article 32.
 
• The High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It allows the Court to issue writs only against the Central Government.**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as writs can be issued against both the **Central Government**, **State Governments**, and even private individuals or entities where applicable.

questions.question: The Union Council of Ministers in India, as the Chief Executive Organ, implicates which of the following?

options.text: Ministers leave all work operations to be done by civil servants
Centralisation of power in local bodies
Each minister is the political head of his/her ministry
The abolition of the role of the Secretary

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Each minister is the political head of his/her ministry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Council of Ministers** is the executive authority in India, responsible for the administration of the country under the guidance of the Prime Minister.
 
• Each minister is designated as the **political head of his/her ministry**, meaning they are responsible for setting policies, making decisions, and ensuring the implementation of laws within their respective departments.
 
• Ministers work in collaboration with **civil servants** who are tasked with operational execution, providing expertise, and implementing policies laid down by the government.
 
• The political leadership of ministers ensures that the actions of their ministry align with the government’s vision and objectives, as well as the interests of the public.
 
• This structure is derived from the **Westminster system**, where the ministers are accountable to the legislature and indirectly to the public.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers operates under the framework of the **Indian Constitution**, particularly Articles **74** and **75**, which define its composition, functions, and roles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministers leave all work operations to be done by civil servants**__

 __
 
• While civil servants play a crucial role in the **implementation of policies**, ministers do not leave all operations to them. Ministers act as the **political heads**, guiding the civil servants in alignment with government goals.
 
 
 
• **Centralisation of power in local bodies**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because the Union Council of Ministers is responsible for **national-level governance**, not local bodies. Local governance is handled by **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and urban municipal bodies under the provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **The abolition of the role of the Secretary**__
 
 
• The role of the Secretary is integral in ministries. Secretaries are **senior civil servants** who assist ministers by providing expertise, advice, and administrative support.
 
• They ensure the smooth functioning of ministries and the execution of policy decisions.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution states about the establishment of Election Commission in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 324**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**.
 
• The Election Commission is responsible for the **superintendence, direction, and control** of elections to the Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of the President and Vice-President of India.
 
• This article vests the power of conducting free and fair elections in an **independent constitutional body**, ensuring the democratic framework of the country.
 
• The Election Commission is a **permanent and independent body** to ensure that elections are conducted in a fair and unbiased manner.
 
• The Commission consists of the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** and other Election Commissioners as the President may appoint.
 
• The powers and functions under Article 324 ensure **autonomy and authority** to the Election Commission to maintain the integrity of the electoral process in India.
 
• It is a vital provision to safeguard the principle of **free and fair elections**, which is the cornerstone of a democratic system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 326**__

 __
 
• **Article 326** deals with the **elections to the House of the People** and to the Legislative Assemblies of States based on **adult suffrage**.
 
• It provides that every citizen who is not less than **18 years** of age and is not otherwise disqualified under the Constitution or law is entitled to vote.
 
 
 
• **Article 325**__
 __
 
• **Article 325** prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, or sex** in the electoral process.
 
• It ensures that no person is ineligible for inclusion in the electoral rolls on these discriminatory grounds.
 
 
 
• **Article 327**__
 
 
• **Article 327** gives the Parliament the power to make laws with respect to all matters relating to **elections to the Legislature**.
 
• This includes the preparation of electoral rolls, the conduct of elections, and any other related matters.

questions.question: Which body took suo motu cognisance of the news titled 'Experts are alarmed as 350 turtles was ashore dead till January 15', published on 16 January 2025?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**National Green Tribunal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** is a specialized judicial body established under the **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**.
 
• Its primary purpose is to handle cases related to **environmental protection** and the conservation of forests and other natural resources.
 
• The NGT has the authority to take **suo motu cognisance** of environmental issues, which means it can initiate action on its own based on media reports or other information, as in the case of the news about **350 turtles found dead on the shore**.
 
• Such cases are critical for addressing violations of environmental laws and ensuring compliance with the principles of **sustainable development** and **environmental justice**.
 
• The tribunal is empowered to provide relief, compensation, and restitution of property and the environment in such cases.
 
• The NGT operates in a **time-bound manner** to ensure swift disposal of cases and is guided by principles of **natural justice**.
 
• This tribunal has jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to the environment is involved, including those arising under laws like the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980**, and **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supreme Court of India**__

 __
 
• The **Supreme Court** is the highest judicial authority in India, established under **Article 124** of the Constitution.
 
• It primarily deals with constitutional matters, appeals from lower courts, and cases of national importance.
 
• While the Supreme Court can address environmental issues, it does not typically take suo motu cognisance of specific environmental cases like the NGT does.
 
 
 
• **High Court of Tamil Nadu**__
 __
 
• The **High Court of Tamil Nadu** is the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in Tamil Nadu and handles cases under its territorial jurisdiction.
 
• Though High Courts can hear environmental cases, they generally do not have the specialized expertise or mandate of the NGT for addressing environmental violations.
 
 
 
• **High Court of Odisha**__
 
 
• The **High Court of Odisha** is the highest judicial body in the state of Odisha.
 
• It can hear cases concerning environmental issues within its state jurisdiction but lacks the pan-India jurisdiction and specialized focus of the NGT.

questions.question: The 9th Amendment Act, 1960, was enacted to give effect to which of the following agreements?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Indo-Pak Agreement, 1958**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **9th Amendment Act, 1960**, was enacted to implement the provisions of the **Indo-Pak Agreement, 1958**.
 
• This agreement dealt with the **transfer of certain territories** between India and Pakistan to address boundary disputes.
 
• The Act amended the **First Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, which lists the territories of the Indian Union.
 
• It resulted in the transfer of **Berubari Union** to Pakistan and the acquisition of certain territories by India in return.
 
• The 1958 agreement was signed to resolve disputes that arose after the **Partition of India in 1947**.
 
• The Act reflects India's commitment to maintaining **peaceful relations** with its neighboring countries through diplomatic means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lahore Declaration, 1999**__

 __
 
• The **Lahore Declaration** was a bilateral agreement and governance treaty signed in **February 1999** between India and Pakistan.
 
• It aimed to improve relations and reduce the risk of conflict, particularly in the context of **nuclear weapons**.
 
• This declaration emphasized **peace, security, and mutual respect** between the two nations.
 
 
 
• **Shimla Agreement, 1972**__
 __
 
• The **Shimla Agreement** was signed in **July 1972** following the **Indo-Pak War of 1971**, which resulted in the creation of Bangladesh.
 
• It aimed to establish long-term peace and resolve disputes through **bilateral discussions**.
 
• The agreement emphasizes the importance of respecting the **Line of Control (LoC)** in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Tashkent Agreement, 1966**__
 
 
• The **Tashkent Agreement** was signed between India and Pakistan in **January 1966** after the **Indo-Pak War of 1965**.
 
• It was mediated by the then-Soviet Union and aimed at restoring **normal relations** between the two countries.
 
• The agreement involved commitments to **withdraw forces** to pre-war positions and resolve disputes peacefully.

questions.question: 5 What specific provision concerning the President of India is outlined in Article 59(3) of the Constitution of India?

options.text: Salary and privileges of the President

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Salary and privileges of the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article **59(3)** of the Constitution of India specifies provisions regarding the **salary, allowances, and privileges** of the President.
 
• The President of India is entitled to a **salary and allowances** that are determined by Parliament.
 
• The President's **official residence**, the Rashtrapati Bhavan, is also provided as part of the privileges.
 
• During their term, the President is entitled to **immunity** from criminal proceedings and cannot be summoned to appear in court.
 
• Article 59 ensures that the President's position is independent and dignified, safeguarding the office from any financial inconvenience.
 
• These provisions are vital to ensure the President can perform their constitutional duties without undue influence or hardship.
 
• Upon retirement, the President is entitled to a **pension**, as specified by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Powers of the President**__

 __
 
• The President of India has extensive powers, including **executive, legislative, and judicial powers.**
 
• Some of these powers include the authority to appoint the **Prime Minister**, approve bills, and declare emergencies under Article 352, 356, and 360.
 
• The President also has the **power to grant pardons** under Article 72.
 
 
 
• **Election of the President**__
 __
 
• The President is elected through an **electoral college** consisting of elected members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies.
 
• The election process is governed by Article **55** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Impeachment of the President**__
 
 
• The President can be removed through a process of **impeachment** under Article **61**.
 
• This process requires a majority in both Houses of Parliament and is conducted for **violation of the Constitution.**

questions.question: The term 'judicial service' under Articles 233-237 refers to:

options.text: District judges and civil judicial posts below them
Only session judges and additional session judges

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,"

__Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'judicial service' under Articles 233-237 of the Indian Constitution is defined as **district judges** and **civil judicial posts below them.**
 
• Judicial service is distinct from executive or administrative posts and is concerned with posts exclusively connected with the administration of justice.
 
• Articles 233-237 specifically deal with provisions for **appointment, conditions of service, and independence of the judiciary** in the subordinate courts.
 
• The appointment of district judges is made by the **Governor of the State** in consultation with the High Court under Article 233.
 
• Other civil judicial posts below the rank of district judge are regulated by Article 234 and are managed by the State Public Service Commission or other prescribed authorities.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 233:** Deals with the appointment of district judges by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.
 
• **Article 234:** Governs recruitment to posts below district judges through methods prescribed by state law.
 
• **Article 235:** Provides for the High Court's control over the subordinate judiciary regarding their posting, promotion, and leave.
 
• **Article 236:** Defines the term 'district judge' and includes various judicial posts such as additional district judges and chief judges of small courts.
 
• **Article 237:** Enables the State to apply provisions of judicial service to magistrates performing judicial functions.

questions.question: Who is responsible for preparing the inaugural speech of the President of India in Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The inaugural speech of the President of India in Parliament is prepared by **The Council of Ministers**, which advises the President on the content of the address.
 
• It is presented at the beginning of the first session of each year or after the formation of a new government.
 
• The speech outlines the government's policies, priorities, and legislative agenda for the upcoming year.
 
• This address is a constitutional requirement under **Article 87 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• It serves as a medium for the government to communicate its vision and plans to the Parliament and the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 87 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It mandates the President to address both Houses of Parliament at the commencement of the first session each year.
 
• The speech is designed to inform the legislature about the government's policies and agenda.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, assists the President in drafting the speech.
 
• This ensures that the address reflects the collective policy decisions and priorities of the government.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Presidential Address:**
 
 
• It sets the tone for parliamentary discussions and debates for the upcoming session.
 
• The address acts as a bridge between the executive branch and the legislative branch of the government.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The tradition of the Presidential Address was inherited from the British parliamentary system.
 
• It underscores the ceremonial significance of the President's role in India's constitutional framework.
